title: truss known-problems catalog, version 1
description: retro/catalog.json, committed in the plugin: problems truss has met before, each with how to recognise it and its known fix. The extractor, factory.ts check, factory.ts doctor and workflows/stage.js report a hit by the entry's id and fix instead of as a new problem (R-25). retro/catalog.ts loadCatalog refuses a file that breaks this schema or has a pattern that does not compile. See adr/0012-self-improving-retro.md, Decision 3.

v.description: File format version. loadCatalog refuses any other v.

entries.description: In match order: a line that hits several entries reports them in this order.

id.description: Stable name, never reused: lowercase words joined by single hyphens.

kind.description: The R-27 kind a recurrence of this entry is reported as.

anchor.description: A literal substring every hit line contains. A line hits the entry only when it contains the anchor and at least one pattern matches it, so a pattern can never hit a line without the anchor.

patterns.description: The entry's signature: JavaScript regular expressions, compiled with new RegExp(p) and no flags, tested against one line of text at a time.

fix.description: The known fix, as the PM or a foreman acts on it. Also the standing ruling factory.ts doctor puts in the bundle when the entry's probe fails.

probe.description: Optional. A host check factory.ts doctor runs on every plan; when it fails, the bundle's rulings get this entry's id and fix. Same shape as a plan need's probe (plan.schema.json $defs.probe).

fixedBy.description: null for a problem no retro has fixed. Otherwise the finding whose fix merged and the date it merged; retro/cli.ts recur then reports each hit of this entry as a recurrence citing it (R-31).

finding.description: The finding id, F-<n>, with the session it came from: <session id>/F-<n>.

run.description: bash -c <run> in the repo; passes on exit 0 within 120 seconds.

path.description: Relative to the repo, or absolute; passes when it exists.
